# flac-lite stream-layer (file-level metadata) golden vectors -- GENERATED
# DO NOT EDIT BY HAND.  Regenerate with:  scripts/gen_stream_vectors.sh
# Generator + independent container walk: scripts/stream_vectors.py
# Frame rows: scripts/frame_vectors.py (find_frames / parse_frame_header)
# Pins: metaflac --list (the reference tool's own block list + field values)
# Encoder: flac 1.5.0
#
# Each `stream_vector` block describes ONE committed fixture in
# tests/fixtures/, byte-for-byte what libFLAC wrote (fixture_len and
# fixture_fnv1a64 pin it -- the same hash the Rust suite reimplements).
# The rows are what tests/stream_metadata_layout.rs asserts
# flac_lite::stream::parse (-> StreamFacts) reports, and none of them comes
# from that code: block types/flags/lengths and every streaminfo field
# are metaflac's, cross-checked at generation time against an
# independent bit-level reading of RFC 9639 section 8 in this file, and
# the frame rows come from the proven strict frame filter (sync shape +
# full field validation + verifying header CRC-8) whose header_bits is
# the same arithmetic the crate's header parser must now reach.
#
# `frame_data_offset` is the byte the frames start at -- the number item
# 4a exists to produce.  `first_frame_hex` is those bytes: enough of the
# real stream to parse its header with the crate's own frame layer, at
# the offset the stream layer reports.  Two layers, one byte offset, no
# hand-built container anywhere (the hand-packed-vector rule, FLAC.md).
#
# `frame_number_forms_*` and `scan_frame_starts_*` are the two
# measurements behind the frame-number strictness rule: every number
# libFLAC wrote here is minimal (so refusing the others is free), and
# the counts say what a scanner sees with and without that rule -- the
# strict count is the frame count, counted by a second independent
# reading of section 9.1 in this file. `mutation*` rows are one real
# frame header of s1 rewritten with its number in each longer form,
# both CRCs recomputed, with the real `flac -d` exit status for each:
# (the frame footer's CRC-16 is measured per frame here to cover the
# frame HEADER as well as the body -- crc16(header+body) equals the
# stored footer, crc16(body) does not -- which is exactly why re-spelling
# a number forces that CRC to be recomputed. An earlier claim in this
# crate that the reference decoder REJECTED the longer form was that
# artifact: a stale CRC, not a structural rule.)
# the reference decoder ACCEPTS those forms (it just never writes
# them), so our refusal is a policy divergence, recorded here rather
# than argued.

stream_vector s1_plain_8k_mono
note two-block container: streaminfo first, a real (empty) Vorbis comment carrying the last-metadata-block flag. No padding, no seektable: --no-padding/--no-seektable are encoder options, so this is libFLAC's own output, not a hand-trimmed file. Also the host of the frame-number FORM mutation (`mutation number-form-overlong`): a frame header of this real stream rewritten with its number in each longer form, both CRCs recomputed — the only witness here that pins what the reference decoder does with a non-minimal form, as opposed to what libFLAC writes.
encode_command flac -1 -f -s --no-padding --no-seektable -b 128 s1_plain_8k_mono.wav -o s1_plain_8k_mono.flac

stream_vector s3_wide_48001hz_b3000
note header width OUTSIDE our packer's 48..=72-bit profile at frame 0: 48001 Hz has no 4-bit sample-rate code (0b1101 appends a 16-bit Hz value, section 9.1.7) and 3000 samples has no 4-bit block-size code (0b0111 appends a 16-bit size-1, section 9.1.6). Both appended forms sit AFTER the coded frame number (Table 13's column order — the same order frame_vectors.py's parser follows), so the FIRST header is 32+8+16+16+8 = 80 bits and both frames here carry 3000/1801, i.e. the 16-bit form twice. Two frames are enough: an appended value form is not tied to frame count, and this is the widest real header this repo commits. Anything wider also needs the frame NUMBER to reach two octets (128+ frames) — measured on a 2.1M-frame synthetic stream (-b 257, 44100 Hz) a single stream contained widths of 80, 88, 96 and 104 bits; that file is not committed (multi-megabyte for a width rule). The format's own ceiling, 128 bits — a 6-octet coded number (the most the 31-bit frame-number bound allows) plus both appended forms plus the CRC — is therefore witnessed by a computed synthetic header in the Rust suite, not by a fixture. Measured: this encode needs no --lax (same as the uncommon-rate streams gen_frame_vectors.sh already encodes) — a wide header is not the same thing as an unstreamable stream. If a future libFLAC stops using the 16-bit forms here, the census below refuses to write.
encode_command flac -1 -f -s --no-padding --no-seektable -b 3000 s3_wide_48001hz_b3000.wav -o s3_wide_48001hz_b3000.flac

stream_vector s4_24bit_8k_mono
note a valid 24-bit stream: the container is ordinary and the reference decoder verifies it, while this crate's decoder carries only 8/16-bit samples (frame.rs bits_per_sample). The stream layer refuses it as UnsupportedSampleSize, so the capability statement has a witness on real bytes rather than a sentence.

stream_vector s5_unseekable_total_unknown
note the same audio as s1, fed as raw s16le PCM through a pipe and encoded to stdout: total samples 0 (unknown), min/max frame size 0 (unknown), MD5 all-zero (unset). `flac -t` still verifies it. This is the fixture that says a decoder may not count frames from total_samples — and the measured reason it exists: piping a WAV is NOT enough, because the WAV header states the sample count before a byte of audio is read, so a piped WAV still declares total_samples (measured, libFLAC 1.5.0). Only raw-in-pipe/pipe-out produces a stream that genuinely declares nothing.
encode_command cat s5_unseekable_total_unknown.raw | flac -1 -f -s --no-padding --no-seektable --force-raw-format --endian=little --sign=signed --sample-rate=8000 --channels=1 --bps=16 -b 128 - > s5_unseekable_total_unknown.flac
